fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase BCC mediator contradicts the observed solidification-segregated, two-BCC-phase microstructure of W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.

The stated 873-1173 K and 0.001-0.1 s^-1 conditions were imported from studies of a different NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy and do not match the target room-temperature compression, room-temperature-to-500 °C indentation, and room-temperature scratch tests.
All cited evidence concerns a composition and processing history different from as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr; it does not support the claimed comparison with commercial powder-sintered tungsten.
The comparison experiment tests overall performance but does not isolate configurational entropy or solid-solution formation as the causal variable.
explanation: The response captures only the broad qualitative expectation that WTaTiVZr can show greater plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten. It misses the actual dual-BCC dendritic structure, applicable temperature window, test methods, quantitative outcomes, and important limits such as residual low-temperature brittleness and the absence of irradiation or operating-fusion validation. Its entropy-based mechanism is generic and insufficient: configurational entropy does not by itself establish either a single phase or improved toughness, and increased resistance to dislocation motion more directly explains strength than plasticity. A causal test would require compositionally or microstructurally controlled variants that separate Ti/V/Zr effects, segregation, phase constitution, and grain structure—not merely tensile testing of the HEA against tungsten.
